Removing the bridge E cuts off the tail, so E tops the table at 66, while the hub C, which the others can route around, scores only 12." width="100%"} Closeness vitality measures a node's importance by computing the change in total graph distances when the node is removed: `vitality(v) = sum_distances(G) - sum_distances(G - v)` Higher values indicate more important/central nodes whose removal would significantly increase average path lengths. Uses parallel BFS with Rayon for efficient computation. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name for the node attribute to store results. If not provided, auto-generates name from method name (`closeness_vitality`). [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns dictionary of results. If `False`, stores results as node attributes and returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to vitality scores. If `return_dict=` is `False`: returns self for method chaining. Higher scores indicate more structurally important nodes. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Closeness vitality (Koschützki et al., 2005) attributes to each node $v$ the change in the graph's *Wiener index* $W(G) = \sum_{u \ne w} d(u, w)$ that would result from removing it: $\mathrm{vit}(v) = W(G) - W(G - v)$. A positive vitality means the network's distances stretch after $v$ is gone, so $v$ was doing important routing work; negative values are rare but possible when a node's removal fragments the graph into components whose pairwise distances no longer count. Computation is inherently expensive at $O(V^2 E / p)$ (one all-pairs shortest-path per node, parallelized across $p$ cores), so plan on staying below a few thousand nodes; degree, PageRank, or betweenness are the usual proxies at scale. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Removing the hub of a star would disconnect every spoke from every other spoke, so it has by far the highest vitality score of the four nodes: ::: {#70fb2c04 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["hub", "A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("hub", "A"), ("hub", "B"), ("hub", "C")]) ) vitality = graph.closeness_vitality(return_dict=True) {graph.get_label_from_id(nid): score for nid, score in vitality.items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'B': 10.0, 'hub': 18.0, 'C': 10.0, 'A': 10.0} ``` ::: :::
